newsitem.title: SPAIN: Key point said agreed in Spain labour reform pact.
newsitem.headline: Key point said agreed in Spain labour reform pact.

text.p: Spanish unions and employers have reached a deal on reducing severance pay, the key sticking point in negotiations on a labour reform pact, newspaper reports said on Saturday.

The papers published the agreement on severance, part of a draft accord currently being drawn up by the two sides. Under the compromise, workers will receive 33 days severance pay for every year worked with a ceiling of 24 months.
Unions have agreed broadly to make it cheaper to fire workers in exchange for a new permanent contract. But the details and final sticking points of the agreement are still being worked out.

A key objective for employers has been to cut dismissal costs which they say are prohibitive and dissuade them from hiring. Unions want a more secure contract, especially for youth who are hardest hit by unemployment.

The government has been pressing for a far-reaching labour reform pact to liberalise Spain's rigid labour market in hopes of bringing down the European Union's highest unemployment rate, more than 20 percent.
Other obstacles to finalising the draft accord remain, including a permanent contract for young workers and long-term unemployed.
